title: Venous thromboembolism risk
blurb: Score VTE risk at booking, on admission and after birth using RCOG GTG 37a as amended in September 2026, and recognise when LMWH is needed and when a clot is suspected.
question: Fatima, 37, BMI 42, smokes and has just had a caesarean section in labour. Using the RCOG risk assessment, what is her postnatal VTE score, and what thromboprophylaxis should be considered?

teach.h: Why VTE matters in maternity care
teach.body: Formally: venous thromboembolism (VTE) is a clot in a deep vein (DVT) that may travel to the lungs (pulmonary embolism, PE). Pregnancy and the puerperium raise the risk. In plain English: clots are the leading cause of maternal death during pregnancy and up to 6 weeks after birth in the UK (MBRRACE-UK 2022-24), and most risk can be spotted with a simple scored checklist. The midwife's role is to score, refer, support LMWH and recognise symptoms.
teach.cite: RCOG GTG 37a (2015, amended 2023) with RCOG position statement Sept 2026; MBRRACE-UK 2022-24

teach.h: Selected risk factor scores (RCOG, amended Sept 2026)
head: Risk factor
Score
rows: Parity 3 or more; smoker; gross varicose veins
PPH over 1 litre or transfusion; prolonged labour over 24 h
Surgery in pregnancy or puerperium; systemic infection; immobility or dehydration
teach.caption: Source: RCOG position statement on GTG 37a, Appendix I (Sept 2026). Immediate perineal repair does not count as surgery.

steps.label: Antenatal score 4+
steps.sub: Consider LMWH from the first trimester

steps.label: Postnatal score 2+
steps.sub: Consider LMWH for at least 10 days

steps.label: Booking BMI 50+
steps.sub: LMWH in pregnancy and 6 weeks postpartum

teach.caption: Admitted antenatally or readmitted in the puerperium: consider thromboprophylaxis. Hyperemesis: offer LMWH and give it within 72 hours.

head: Weight
Enoxaparin
teach.caption: The higher doses may be given in two divided doses. These replace the weight bands in the 2015 guideline.

items: On antenatal LMWH: do not inject further doses if there is vaginal bleeding or once labour begins; reassess on admission.
Avoid regional techniques for at least 12 hours after a prophylactic dose.
No LMWH for 4 hours after a spinal, or after the epidural catheter is removed; do not remove the catheter within 12 hours of the last injection.
Give the first postnatal dose as soon as possible after birth if there is no PPH and no regional analgesia restriction.
LMWH and warfarin are safe with breastfeeding; DOACs are not recommended when breastfeeding.

teach.body: NICE NG194 1.2.4: leg swelling and tenderness, or shortness of breath, could indicate VTE; chest pain could indicate VTE or a cardiac problem. Teach these at the first postnatal contact. If the midwife suspects a DVT or PE, she arranges urgent medical assessment the same day; with breathlessness, chest pain or collapse this is an emergency. Encourage mobility and hydration, as immobility and dehydration are risk factors in their own right.

teach.h: Worked scenario: Fatima after her caesarean
teach.body: Fatima scores: age over 35 = 1, BMI 40-49 = 2, smoker = 1, caesarean in labour = 2. Total 6. A postnatal score of 2 or more means LMWH should be considered for at least 10 days. Her weight decides the enoxaparin dose (for example 60 mg daily if 100-129 kg). If she had a spinal, or an epidural catheter that is removed, the first dose waits at least 4 hours. The midwife explains why, teaches injection technique and the warning signs.
teach.cite: RCOG position statement (Sept 2026) Appendix I and Table 1; GTG 37a

teach.text: The Sept 2026 RCOG amendment changed BMI scoring: BMI 40-49 now scores 2 and BMI 50 or more scores 4, and booking BMI 50+ means LMWH antenatally AND for 6 weeks postnatally. Do not use the old 2015 weight bands for doses.

items: Assess in early pregnancy, on any admission, and intrapartum or immediately after birth.
Postnatal score 2 or more: consider LMWH for at least 10 days.
Booking BMI 50+: LMWH in pregnancy and 6 weeks postpartum; previous VTE: at least 6 weeks postpartum.
Hyperemesis scores 3: offer LMWH within 72 hours.
No LMWH within 4 hours of a spinal or epidural catheter removal; LMWH is safe with breastfeeding.

summary: You can now score VTE risk with the amended RCOG tool at booking, admission and after birth, and know when LMWH is considered and for how long. You can time LMWH around regional anaesthesia and recognise symptoms of DVT and PE that need urgent assessment.

A.q: When should a woman first have a documented VTE risk assessment in pregnancy, according to RCOG GTG 37a?
options: At the 28-week antenatal appointment
On admission to the labour ward
At the 20-week anomaly scan visit
In early pregnancy or prepregnancy
A.why: GTG 37a: all women should undergo a documented assessment of risk factors for VTE in early pregnancy or prepregnancy, repeated on admission and intrapartum or immediately postpartum.

whyNot.0: 28 weeks is when LMWH is considered for an antenatal score of 3, not the first assessment.
whyNot.1: Admission in labour is a repeat assessment point; the first is in early pregnancy.
whyNot.2: The anomaly scan is not the VTE assessment point.

A.q: Under the September 2026 RCOG amendment, what thromboprophylaxis should a woman with a booking BMI of 52 be offered?
options: LMWH for at least 10 days after the birth
LMWH from 28 weeks of pregnancy until birth
Antenatal LMWH and 6 weeks postpartum
Anti-embolism stockings during labour
A.why: RCOG position statement (Sept 2026): women with a booking BMI of 50 or more should be offered LMWH during pregnancy and for 6 weeks postpartum, in line with the NHS England Maternal Care Bundle.

whyNot.0: 10 days is the postnatal course for a score of 2 or more; BMI 50+ needs 6 weeks postpartum plus antenatal LMWH.
whyNot.1: Starting at 28 weeks applies to an antenatal score of 3 and does not cover the postnatal period.
whyNot.3: Stockings are for women who cannot have LMWH because of bleeding risk, not instead of LMWH here.

A.q: Which postnatal VTE score means the midwife should expect LMWH to be considered for at least 10 days?
options: 2 or more
1 or more
3 or more
4 or more
A.why: RCOG Appendix I (amended Sept 2026): if the total score is 2 or more postnatally, consider thromboprophylaxis for at least 10 days.

whyNot.1: A score of 1 does not reach the postnatal threshold.
whyNot.2: 3 is the antenatal threshold for considering LMWH from 28 weeks.
whyNot.3: 4 is the antenatal threshold for LMWH from the first trimester; the postnatal threshold is lower.

B.q: Jess, 30, BMI 24, non-smoker, para 1, had an elective caesarean for breech with no other risk factors. What is her postnatal VTE score?
B.why: Elective caesarean birth scores 1 and she has no other listed risk factors, so her total is 1. Below 2, LMWH is not routinely indicated; encourage mobility and hydration.

whyNot.0: An elective caesarean scores 1, so her total is not zero.
whyNot.1: Caesarean in labour scores 2; an elective caesarean scores 1.
whyNot.2: 4 is the score for surgery in pregnancy or the puerperium, not a planned caesarean birth.

B.q: Mia, 28, had an epidural in labour. The catheter was removed at 14:00. When is the earliest she can have her first postnatal prophylactic LMWH dose?
options: 14:00, as the catheter is out
02:00 the next day
B.why: GTG 37a: LMWH should not be given for 4 hours after the epidural catheter has been removed, so the earliest is 18:00.

whyNot.0: Giving LMWH at catheter removal breaches the 4-hour gap.
whyNot.1: 2 hours is shorter than the 4-hour gap required.
whyNot.3: 12 hours is the interval between the last LMWH dose and catheter removal, not the wait after removal.

B.q: Lola, 26, is 10 weeks pregnant and admitted with hyperemesis: she cannot keep fluids down. What does the RCOG September 2026 position statement recommend about VTE prophylaxis?
options: Offer LMWH and give it within 72 hours
Wait until 28 weeks before considering LMWH
Start LMWH after she is discharged home
Use stockings, as LMWH is unsafe this early
B.why: The RCOG statement follows the NHS England Maternal Care Bundle: women with hyperemesis should be offered LMWH and receive it within 72 hours; continue for the duration of the risk and for a further week after it resolves.

whyNot.1: Hyperemesis scores 3 and is a transient risk factor needing prompt LMWH, not waiting until 28 weeks.
whyNot.2: The risk is highest while she is admitted and immobile, so LMWH starts during the admission.
whyNot.3: LMWH is used in early pregnancy; stockings are for women with bleeding risk.

C.q: Grace, 38, para 3 (now para 4), BMI 33, had a vaginal birth after 26 hours of labour and lost 1.3 litres. What is her postnatal score and the most likely plan?
options: Score 3: no LMWH, mobilise
Score 5: LMWH for at least 10 days
Score 5: LMWH for 6 weeks postpartum
Score 4: LMWH until discharge home
C.why: Age over 35 = 1, parity 3 or more = 1, BMI 30-39 = 1, prolonged labour over 24 hours = 1, PPH over 1 litre = 1: total 5. A postnatal score of 2 or more means considering LMWH for at least 10 days. The first dose should wait until any PPH is controlled.

whyNot.0: She has five scoring factors, not three, and any postnatal score of 2 or more meets the threshold.
whyNot.2: 6 weeks postnatally is for previous VTE, booking BMI 50+ or high antenatal scores; her plan is at least 10 days.
whyNot.3: Her score is 5, and LMWH continues for at least 10 days, not just until discharge.

C.q: Hope, 32, takes prophylactic LMWH in pregnancy because of a previous VTE. At 39 weeks she phones to say her waters have broken and contractions have started. What should the midwife advise about her next LMWH dose?
options: Inject tonight's dose now, before she comes in
Halve the dose and inject it later this evening
Inject as usual, then come in after 12 hours
Do not inject; she is reassessed on admission
C.why: GTG 37a: women on antenatal LMWH should not inject any further doses if they have vaginal bleeding or once labour begins; they are reassessed on admission and further doses prescribed by medical staff.

whyNot.0: Injecting at labour onset may prevent regional analgesia and increase bleeding risk.
whyNot.1: Dose reduction at home is not the GTG 37a advice; she should not inject once labour begins.
whyNot.2: Delaying admission for 12 hours in labour is unsafe, and she should not inject.

C.q: Kate, 34, had a DVT in a previous pregnancy and is now breastfeeding after a normal birth. The obstetrician proposes postnatal anticoagulation. Which plan fits GTG 37a?
options: A DOAC for 10 days, compatible with breastfeeding
Aspirin for 6 weeks, as LMWH affects breast milk
LMWH or warfarin for at least 6 weeks postpartum
LMWH for 10 days, as she had a vaginal birth
C.why: GTG 37a: all women with a previous confirmed VTE should be offered LMWH or warfarin for at least 6 weeks postpartum regardless of mode of birth. LMWH and warfarin are safe in breastfeeding.

whyNot.0: DOACs are not recommended when breastfeeding.
whyNot.1: Aspirin is not the recommended VTE prophylaxis, and LMWH is safe with breastfeeding.
whyNot.3: Previous VTE needs at least 6 weeks, whatever the mode of birth.

reteach.title: Count the points, then read the dial
reteach.question: Think of the RCOG tool as adding points onto a dial. What do the points mean after the birth?

blocks.body: Every risk factor adds points: 1 for things like age over 35, smoking, parity 3+, BMI 30-39; 2 for BMI 40-49 or caesarean in labour; 4 for BMI 50+, previous VTE or a transient factor like surgery or systemic infection. After birth the dial has one key mark: 2 points or more means LMWH should be considered for at least 10 days.

blocks.text: Caesarean IN LABOUR scores 2, ELECTIVE caesarean scores 1. Read the stem carefully for when the caesarean happened.

explain.body: A documented VTE risk assessment in early pregnancy or prepregnancy, repeated on any admission or intercurrent problem, and again intrapartum or immediately postpartum.

test.q: Lily, 29, is admitted at 30 weeks with pyelonephritis needing IV antibiotics. What should happen to her VTE assessment?
options: Keep the booking score unchanged until the birth
Repeat it, adding 4 for systemic infection
Repeat it after she is discharged
Recalculate it at the 36-week visit
test.why: GTG 37a: repeat the risk assessment on any admission. A current systemic infection needing IV antibiotics or admission scores 4 as a transient factor (RCOG Appendix I, Sept 2026).

whyNot.0: The score must be repeated on admission, not kept from booking.
whyNot.2: The risk is present now, during the admission.
whyNot.3: Waiting until 36 weeks misses the period of highest risk.

explain.body: Postnatal score 2 or more: consider LMWH for at least 10 days. Previous VTE: at least 6 weeks postpartum. Booking BMI 50+: antenatal LMWH and 6 weeks postpartum.

test.q: Which woman needs postnatal LMWH for at least 6 weeks?
options: Postnatal score of 2 after an elective caesarean
Previous confirmed DVT, now after a vaginal birth
Age 36 with a BMI of 31 and no other factors
Pre-eclampsia in this pregnancy and a current smoker
test.why: GTG 37a: previous confirmed VTE means LMWH or warfarin for at least 6 weeks postpartum regardless of mode of birth.

whyNot.0: A score of 2 means considering LMWH for at least 10 days.
whyNot.2: Age over 35 and BMI 30-39 score 2: at least 10 days.
whyNot.3: Pre-eclampsia and smoking score 2: at least 10 days.

explain.body: Avoid regional techniques for at least 12 hours after a prophylactic LMWH dose. No LMWH for 4 hours after a spinal or after epidural catheter removal; do not remove the catheter within 12 hours of the last injection.

head: Event
Gap
rows: Last prophylactic dose to regional block
Spinal or catheter removal to next dose

test.q: Which gap is required between removing an epidural catheter and giving prophylactic LMWH?
options: 4 hours
1 hour
12 hours
24 hours
test.why: GTG 37a: LMWH should not be given for 4 hours after the epidural catheter has been removed.

whyNot.1: 1 hour is shorter than the 4-hour gap.
whyNot.2: 12 hours is the gap between the last LMWH dose and catheter removal.
whyNot.3: 24 hours applies to avoiding regional techniques after a therapeutic dose.

explain.body: LMWH and warfarin are safe in breastfeeding; DOACs are not recommended. Teach that leg swelling and tenderness, breathlessness or chest pain need medical advice without delay.

test.q: Ana, 31, is on postnatal LMWH and breastfeeding. She asks whether she should stop feeding while on injections. What is the best response?
options: Yes, until the course is finished
Yes, unless she switches to a DOAC
No, but she should express and discard
No, LMWH is safe with breastfeeding
test.why: GTG 37a: LMWH and warfarin are safe in breastfeeding, so she can continue feeding normally.

whyNot.0: There is no need to stop breastfeeding on LMWH.
whyNot.1: DOACs are not recommended when breastfeeding.
whyNot.2: Expressing and discarding milk is unnecessary with LMWH.
